content:
#40207 added a feature to revoke bors delegations if pushes after the delegation touch sensitive files. It also says:

(bors will do its best to distinguish from changes to the code coming from the `master`
branch so except in cases of PRs that touch a large number of files,
merging `master` should be safe, even if there are changes outside the above directories.)

#39106 changes just 4 files, and merging master revoked the delegation.
Does anyone have examples where merging master (with changes to sensitive files) did not revoke the delegation, or is the above note wrong? (or maybe there's a bug with the detection)

Separately, I'm really unsure of the benefits of this feature and if they're worth preventing master merges.
I'll reiterate the question I asked on #40207:
Can you please elaborate on the goal with it? Is it to protect the CI servers or other contributors who have cloned the project?

cc @Bryan Gin-ge Chen
(posting here and not in #ecosystem infrastructure for visibility)

I'll take a look. This is definitely unintended.

The goal of this is to improve security: if someone is delegated and their github account gets hacked, an attacker could merge changes to scripts and workflows that could compromise the integrity of the cache and put users at risk.

A malicious contributor (or a hacked contributor) can modify Mathlib/init.lean or any other lean file to do an rm -rf / on the user's computer, so preventing changes to scripts/ is redundant.
I think the same goes for the cache, as Mathlib/Init.lean runs inside the lake build that creates the oleans, so code there could modify the oleans however they want before uploading to the cache.

What is the attack vector that this change guards against?
My understanding is "defense in depth". Make it harder, security is a process. (Bryan will know much more.)

And indeed, poisoning the cache by uploading code to a PR (that makes other download these files on innocuous changes) should not be possible. Any loopholes are bugs to fix. (I'm not aware of any right now.)
Changes to files in Mathlib (and the whitelisted paths) run inside a sandbox when we're building the cache in CI. We need to be much more careful about those outside.

I've deployed a change to bors that should prevent this from happening again (bors-ng#52). Merging master into PRs that touch > 3000 files is still likely to expire delegations due to "too many files changed", so I'll keep investigating to see if there's a way around the GitHub API limitations we're hitting here.
